about: Public facts imported from PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website (by-place research and mapped companies) by scripts/import-website.mjs. Each value keeps the source and the date read that the Website team recorded.

entries.name: Alcoutim Business Park (Parque Empresarial de Alcoutim)
entries.what: The council's industrial estate: 54,320 square metres in 26 lots, 23 of them for industrial units, between the EN 122, the EN 124 and the new IC27, about 30 kilometres from the coast and Spain and about 6 kilometres from the town. The council publishes the park's regulation as a PDF on the same page, and the page is dated 4 November 2025.

entries.name: Celeiro de Ideias business and coworking centre (planned)
entries.what: A future centre for microbusinesses, freelancers, startups and artisans in the former EPAC granary, with entrepreneurship support services. Works are due to finish on 30 September 2028, so it is not open yet.

entries.name: Algarve 2030 territorial incentive scheme (SIBT), notice ALGARVE-2026-5
entries.what: A 5 million euro call for micro and small companies to create, expand or modernise, with up to 60 percent co-financing and special weight for inland, low-density territories. Priority areas include digitalisation and information and communication technologies. Applications are open until 15 January 2027, assessed in rounds ending 30 July, 30 October 2026 and 15 January 2027. The council posts the notice on its own site.

entries.name: Algarve 2030 regional programme (FEDER) in the Celeiro de Ideias centre
entries.what: EU regional funding for the council's business and coworking centre.

entries.name: Fundacao Galp (Vilas em Movimento)
entries.what: Social investment in Alcoutim's shared electric bikes, with the Odiana association and the council.
entries.amount: more than 100,000 euros for the bike system

entries.name: Interreg Spain-Portugal and FEDER in Agrosocial Plus
entries.what: Cross-border funding of the project in which Odiana represents the Lower Guadiana and Living Labs will test AI and IoT.
entries.amount: 1,546,822.39 euros of 2,062,429.85 euros in total, for the whole project

entries.name: PRR funding for the Algarve 6.0 Smart Territorial Hub
entries.what: Non-refundable PRR funding for the six-municipality sensor and data platform.

entries.name: Algarve 2030 (FEDER) in the council's digitisation project
entries.what: EU regional funding for digital infrastructure, online services and cybersecurity at the council.

entries.name: LeiGPT
entries.what: AI platform for lawyers on Portuguese law, registered in Faro and a member of Algarve Evolution, which its site lists with Google for Startups and Akamai among its partners and supporters. It answers legal research questions with citations to codes and court rulings, analyses documents, and runs as a cloud service or on a client's own servers. Available now, with a free one-day trial.

entries.name: Bot Gonçalves
entries.what: Venture Lab by AlgarveSTP company that uses AI and satellite imagery to monitor critical infrastructure. The article gives no town: needs a primary source.

entries.name: Cais do Porto (Aveiro)
entries.what: A hub in Aveiro that selects Brazilian technology firms to set up in the city. Its June 2026 batch added ten firms and its 22 incubated startups demo at Aveiro Tech Week.

entries.name: PCI Rocket Booster Acceleration (with startUP23, supported by Turismo de Portugal)
entries.what: Acceleration programme of the University of Aveiro's science park for startups, including AI solutions for tourism, smart destinations and mobility. The 2026 call's status is unclear on the page.

entries.name: Incubadora de Empresas da Câmara Municipal de Aveiro
entries.what: The council's incubator, created in 2017 under its entrepreneurship policy and part of the IERA network. It has 6 individual offices, a coworking space, a meeting room, Wi-Fi and a printer, and gives members access to the congress auditorium (224 people) and the Salão Nobre (60 people). It sits at the Parque de Exposições. The page does not say who can apply or how, and does not mention AI.

entries.name: Bairro Comercial Digital de Aveiro (council pilot)
entries.what: A council pilot area for digitalising local businesses, to help owners, merchants, workers and consumers through digital tools. Local merchants can ask for more information through a form on the page. A route for shops, not for AI startups; the page does not mention AI.

entries.name: Portugal 2020 funding for Augmanity
entries.what: 8.5 million euros of the 20 million euro Augmanity project came from European funds through Portugal 2020. The project included a machine-learning subproject and ended around 2023.

entries.name: Huawei into the 5GAIner lab
entries.what: Huawei funds the 5G and AI reliability lab and donated its equipment, under a 2020 protocol with UA and the Instituto de Telecomunicações.

entries.name: Urban Innovative Actions (EU) into Aveiro STEAM City
entries.what: Aveiro STEAM City is a council-led project of about 6.1 million euros, with 4.9 million euros of EU funding from the Urban Innovative Actions programme. Partners include Altice Labs, the Instituto de Telecomunicações, the University of Aveiro, INOVARIA and CEDES. It builds 5G and IoT infrastructure; the page does not mention AI. Aveiro's bid was one of 22 chosen from 184. The page gives no date.

entries.name: Madrix
entries.what: Brazilian firm selected for Cais do Porto in Aveiro in June 2026. Builds and runs custom corporate applications with AI.

entries.name: Sião
entries.what: Brazilian firm at Cais do Porto in Aveiro. Offers solutions for notary offices with AI and data protection.

entries.name: Stepps
entries.what: Brazilian firm at Cais do Porto in Aveiro. Uses AI and video analysis to turn industrial cameras into monitoring tools.

entries.name: Sherlock
entries.what: Brazilian firm at Cais do Porto in Aveiro. Offers advanced data analysis and AI for investigations and decisions in the public sector.

entries.name: Beja council: Espaço Empresa
entries.what: The council's one-stop point for entrepreneurs and companies, giving information, advice and follow-up. It lists online company formation, admissibility certificates for a company name, commercial registry changes, SME certification, a digital mobile key and trademark services. It publishes in-person, phone, email and online channels. The page names no incubator.

entries.name: CIBT NERBE, Beja's technology incubator
entries.what: Run by the business association NERBE/AEBAL. Second phase: 13 modular offices of 24 to 40 square metres, a coworking room with up to six workstations, meeting rooms and parking. Open to companies, entrepreneurs and investors in food and forestry, water, ICT and aeronautics, with young and qualified people a priority. Apply with a manifestation-of-interest form and read the incubation regulation, both linked from its page.

entries.name: NERBE/AEBAL: Ninho de Empresas and business support
entries.what: The Beja business association, active since 1987, lists business and legal advice, training and consulting, project support, internationalisation help and facility rental. Its menu also names a Ninho de Empresas (business nest), with no details on the page we read.

entries.name: Beja council: Financiamento
entries.what: The council's page lists the funding programmes it points to, including PRR, COMPETE 2020, Alentejo 2020, INTERREG, Turismo de Portugal and the European Investment Bank. It is a list of names, with no call or deadline.

entries.name: Startup Portugal
entries.what: The national startup agency offers, on its homepage, the Road 2 Web Summit, Business Abroad and Tech Foundry Portugal Deep Tech Edition programmes and a one-stop shop for founders. The page does not mention Beja, so this is a national route open to a Beja founder, not a local one.

entries.name: Promove programme (Fundação la Caixa and BPI, with the FCT) into SiARA
entries.what: The SiARA AI and field-robot project, with the Beja polytechnic as a partner, was recognised in the programme's 7th edition in the mobilising R&D projects category. The article gives no amount.

entries.name: InnoWave's own AI investment
entries.what: A company's self-funded plan, not outside capital: 2.2 million euros in 2024 and 2025 and 1.6 million planned for 2026.

entries.name: Alentejo 2030 into the second phase of CIBT NERBE
entries.what: A search summary said the second phase was approved with over 2 million euros of investment. We opened only the incubator's own page, which shows the second-phase spaces and not the amount, so treat the figure as unconfirmed.

entries.name: Startup Braga
entries.what: InvestBraga's innovation hub with pre-acceleration (Startup Point), an acceleration programme and incubation. Its focus areas are nanotechnology, health technologies, digital economy, biotechnology and sustainability.

entries.name: InvestBraga
entries.what: The municipality's economic development agency, which also runs the Startup Braga hub and works on attracting companies to Braga.

entries.name: Startup Portugal: One Stop Shop and programmes
entries.what: The national startup agency's page lists a One Stop Shop for founders covering funding, visas and programmes, plus programmes such as Road 2 Web Summit. Its events are in Lisbon and Porto only and the page does not mention Braga.

entries.name: Empresa na Hora (Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado)
entries.what: The state counter service that creates quota companies, single-member companies and public limited companies at once. The gov.pt page names the counter route and does not list steps, documents or fees, and we did not find a Braga counter page.

entries.name: GED Ventures (GED Tech Seed fund) and Portugal Ventures into PluggableAI
entries.what: A 1.75 million euro seed round for a Braga startup incubated at Startup Braga, after a 100,000 euro pre-seed.

entries.name: HCapital, with Bright Pixel and Armilar Venture Partners, into Automaise
entries.what: A 1 million euro seed round for a Braga AI automation platform.

entries.name: EIT Community AI Challenge prize to Braga and Hayden AI
entries.what: A European Institute of Innovation and Technology AI challenge prize that funded the bus-camera pilot. The amount is not stated on the pages we read.

entries.name: Norte 2030 into Intelligence4Administration
entries.what: About 1.5 million euros of regional programme money for the council's project to bring AI into municipal administration.

entries.name: PRR (via IAPMEI) into dotmoovs
entries.what: A 30,000 euro non-repayable PRR grant to a Braga company for its digital sports network. The register lists Braga as the only municipality funded.

entries.name: OmniumAI
entries.what: Spin-off of UMinho's Centre of Biological Engineering. It coordinates IngredientIA and has built the CibusAI platform, to be extended for the project.

entries.name: Hayden AI
entries.what: Startup whose camera system ran on two Braga buses for the council and TUB. The article quotes a company representative and does not state its base city.

entries.name: PluggableAI
entries.what: Startup founded in 2022, incubated at Startup Braga. Its Fanmeter product uses AI and non-intrusive sensors for fan engagement and has been used by Sporting Clube de Braga and Rock in Rio. Raised a 1.75 million euro seed round in September 2024.

entries.name: dotmoovs
entries.what: Braga startup (the press says founded December 2024) whose app uses AI on phone video to analyse exercise movements and aims to help spot sports talent.

entries.name: Automaise
entries.what: Braga company with a cloud, low-code AI platform for voice, chat and inbox automation. A 2021 article reports a 1 million euro seed round and 14 staff. We found nothing newer.

entries.name: ASOagentAI
entries.what: Startup in the Startup Braga ecosystem at Web Summit 2026 with an AI agent that gets app installs and revenue. The accelerator's news list also shows ASOagent among the winners of its 10th acceleration programme in June 2026.

entries.name: eDynamics
entries.what: Startup in the Startup Braga ecosystem at Web Summit 2026 that combines biomechanics and AI to turn movement data into injury-risk alerts.

entries.name: LogisticsWMS
entries.what: Startup in the Startup Braga ecosystem at Web Summit 2026 with an AI-based warehouse management system.

entries.name: Zixago
entries.what: Startup in the Startup Braga ecosystem at Web Summit 2026 described as synthetic infrastructure for AI.

entries.name: Bragança council: Gabinete de Apoio ao Investidor
entries.what: The council's investor support office gives personal guidance on investment intentions in the municipality, speeds up the internal steps for installation and licensing, helps set up R&D cooperation networks and looks for funding lines.

entries.name: Espaço Empresa de Bragança (IAPMEI, at Brigantia EcoPark)
entries.what: A face-to-face business counter opened on 16 April 2018 inside the science park, run by IAPMEI with partner agencies and the council. It handles Balcão do Empreendedor and Portal do Cidadão operations such as company creation, name requests, permanent certificates and registrations. Weekday hours are published on the page.

entries.name: Bragança council: municipal investment incentives
entries.what: The council does not charge the municipal surtax (derrama) on the taxable profits of companies headquartered in Bragança, and has a regulation granting tax incentives to investments of municipal interest. The page gives no amounts.

entries.name: Licenciamento Zero and the Balcão do Empreendedor (council guide)
entries.what: The council's guide to opening an establishment with a prior communication and electronic form on the Balcão do Empreendedor, with the municipal forms for installation, changes, opening hours and public-space use. It covers shops and restaurants, not a tech company's incorporation.

entries.name: Poliempreende (polytechnic ideas competition)
entries.what: The polytechnic's regional business-ideas contest drew 75 projects in its 22nd edition in 2026, from students and from researchers at CeDRI and CIMO, with mentoring from the polytechnic's entrepreneurship and employability office before the final. The report does not give the prizes.

entries.name: Polytechnic and Paraná universities: startup acceleration programme
entries.what: A memorandum signed on 12 March 2026 with six state and federal universities in Paraná, Brazil, lets startups run joint research and innovation projects, join international mobility and reach incubation, mentoring and market networks. The report gives no application steps.

entries.name: Brigantia EcoPark
entries.what: Science and technology park for consolidated and incubated technology-based companies, with laboratory space, run by a private non-profit association. The council's page names energy, environment and eco-construction as its areas. No application route or price is published on the pages we read. A December 2025 report says it is about 98 percent occupied and is tendering a second phase.

entries.name: AI4PA Portugal EDIH
entries.what: Offers testing, training, networking and funding advice for public bodies and SMEs adopting AI, with a discount on contracted services under the project.

entries.name: Brigantia EcoPark 2 design tender (park board, chaired by the council's mayor)
entries.what: The park's board approved on 5 December 2025 a public tender with a base price of 308,000 euros plus VAT for the execution project of a second phase, to add capacity and attract technology investment. The page does not name the funder of the build.

entries.name: PRR equipment grant to CeDRI (polytechnic)
entries.what: A 474,097.74 euro PRR grant for equipment, ended 30 June 2026, with smart industrial applications among its expected results.

entries.name: Council: InvestCB and the Investidor page
entries.what: The council's investment strategy names five industrial axes, including information technology and aeronautics, and announced a Balcão do Investidor on its site. It lists an industrial incubator in the business location area.

entries.name: Council: Balcão do Empreendedor (Espaço Empresa)
entries.what: The council's page on the national electronic single counter for starting and running a business, with Licenciamento Zero explained.

entries.name: CEi, Centro de Empresas Inovadoras
entries.what: Council-run centre with pre-incubation space without forming a company, subsidised incubation services, business development support for R&D units and consultancy for startups and SMEs.

entries.name: StartUp.CB, the polytechnic's incubator
entries.what: Infrastructure, mentor networks, training and personalised follow-up for technology-based startups, with a published regulation and an information channel at the I9 office.

entries.name: Boost@IPCB proof-of-concept contest (INOVC+)
entries.what: Selected 4 research projects with 4,500 euros each, 18,000 euros in total, to move them to technology readiness levels 4 and 5. Open to staff, researchers and entrepreneurs of the polytechnic.

entries.name: Poliempreende (22nd edition, 2026)
entries.what: Polytechnic entrepreneurship contest with workshops on markets and business plans, a regional jury on 24 June 2026 and regional prizes of 2,000 and 1,500 euros.

entries.name: I9@IPCB technology transfer office
entries.what: The polytechnic's office for valuing research and moving it to business, under the INOVC+ project. Its spin-off page lists university spin-offs.

entries.name: Empresa na Hora (national counter)
entries.what: One-stop counter to form a limited company or similar in a single visit, with all partners present.

entries.name: Startup Portugal
entries.what: National startup agency site with a founder's guide, the national incubator network (RNi) and programmes.

entries.name: Portugal 2030 (Centro 2030) and the EU into INOVC+
entries.what: Co-funds the regional innovation ecosystem behind the polytechnic's I9 office and the Boost@IPCB contest, which pays 18,000 euros in prizes.

entries.name: PRR into the polytechnic's incubator Startup Castelo Branco
entries.what: The state's recovery plan transparency portal lists the incubator initiative with a total of 150 thousand euros.

entries.name: Odin Systems, ODIN Defense Hub (private investment in the city)
entries.what: An investment announced by the council as above 40 million euros, to be built in phases, with a Potential National Interest (PIN) application planned.

entries.name: Axtron Systems
entries.what: Startup based in Castelo Branco, founded in 2023 by two professors of the polytechnic, whose FIRECOM tool uses drones and an AI model to plan fire containment strips.

entries.name: Edifício Multifuncional de Empresas (EME), Câmara Municipal de Castro Marim
entries.what: The council's business hub with individual offices, shared spaces, meeting rooms, wireless internet and incubation support, for entrepreneurs with innovative, scalable ideas who want their headquarters in Castro Marim. The council publishes the operating regulation, an application form and an information leaflet.

entries.name: Council online services, regulations and municipal fees
entries.what: The council's online services portal, its regulations in force and its table of municipal fees, linked from the same business page.

entries.name: CRIA, University of Algarve (entrepreneurship and technology transfer)
entries.what: Ran the Atlazul Guadiana business-ideas contest in Castro Marim in 2022, with the council and CCMAR on the jury. No current Castro Marim programme found.

entries.name: SalOS
entries.what: Traceability and operations platform for artisanal salt producers, born inside the Sapal de Castro Marim reserve, with a free 30 day trial. Press describes a digital assistant and a salinity and sluice support tool.

entries.name: GO Coimbra, the city's investment and innovation agency
entries.what: Offers a single point of contact for investors, with help through licensing and soft landing, and help to find sites in its three business parks and coworks. The page also lists a fast-track for investment and an incentives page.

entries.name: Coimbra council: Via Rápida para o Investimento and Invest Coimbra incentives
entries.what: A fast-track request for business investment filed through the council's online services (prior registration needed), plus a regulation of municipal incentives such as partial or full exemption from property transfer tax, property tax for up to five years, local business surtax and urban fees. Projects in innovative or technology-based sectors are among those that can qualify.

entries.name: Coimbra council: Cowork Pátio (creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship)
entries.what: A municipal coworking space in the former Colégio das Artes in the city centre, with shared spaces for new businesses.

entries.name: Coimbra council and Startup Portugal memorandum
entries.what: Signed on 14 November 2024 at Web Summit. The council shares ecosystem information, identifies startups and scaleups recognised by Startup Portugal and based in the municipality, helps attract talent and investors, and publicises its events. No cost to the parties.

entries.name: Instituto Pedro Nunes business incubator
entries.what: Open to any project that develops technology-based products or advanced services, with priority for University of Coimbra spin-offs. Application starts with a free form, then a business plan with IPN support. Physical modules from 20 to 66 square metres, or virtual incubation, plus legal, funding and consultant support.

entries.name: Instituto Pedro Nunes business accelerator
entries.what: Launched in May 2014 for more advanced technology companies with high growth potential, with internationalisation support. By its own count the aggregate impact for 2014 to 2023 covers 42 companies.

entries.name: NATO DIANA accelerator at IPN
entries.what: Defence and dual-use accelerator with 100,000 euros in stage 1 and up to 300,000 in stage 2, access to NATO test centres, mentoring and investor links. Priority areas begin with AI.

entries.name: ESA BIC Centro
entries.what: Incubation for early-stage startups with a space connection, coordinated by IPN in Coimbra, with Coimbra Supernova as the city's space cluster alliance.

entries.name: Startup Portugal: founder resources
entries.what: The national startup agency lists a Founder's Guide, a national incubators network and an investors matching programme. We read only the page's headings, not the guide's content.

entries.name: Empresa na Hora (gov.pt service)
entries.what: The national service to set up private limited and public limited companies quickly at a counter. The responsible entity is the national registry institute. The page does not list Coimbra counters.

entries.name: CoimbraCityLab (council test bed for technology projects)
entries.what: A council initiative to support the development and testing of innovative, technology-based projects in real conditions, open to individuals and to public or private legal entities whose projects meet its regulation. A 2023 pilot with IPN tested an AI product.

entries.name: Lince Capital, Explorer Investments and Armilar Venture Partners into Neuraspace
entries.what: Private backers of Neuraspace's 15.6 million euro round, alongside national recovery plan funds. The page does not split the amounts.

entries.name: National recovery plan (PRR) funds into Neuraspace
entries.what: Public funds that are part of the same round.

entries.name: NATO DIANA initial funding for Neuraspace
entries.what: Neuraspace was one of two Portuguese companies picked for NATO's DIANA accelerator, with access to 100,000 euros of initial investment and later up to 300,000.

entries.name: Feedzai funding round
entries.what: The financial-crime AI company that the map lists in Coimbra raised 75 million dollars on a valuation above 2 billion dollars and signed a framework agreement with the European Central Bank for digital euro fraud detection. The page names no investors.

entries.name: NATO DIANA programme (via the IPN accelerator)
entries.what: Stage 1 funding of 100,000 euros, stage 2 up to 300,000, and a route to the NATO Innovation Fund for defence technology companies.

entries.name: Invest Coimbra municipal incentives
entries.what: Council tax exemptions for investment projects, including innovative and technology-based ones.

entries.name: coalex.ai
entries.what: AI-powered automation with human oversight, listed as an IPN incubator company. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Granter.ai
entries.what: Uses AI to help businesses find and write grant applications, with expert review. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: EDNU.AI
entries.what: Describes itself as an AI development partner. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Sentinel.AI
entries.what: Describes itself as trusted intelligence for critical systems. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Complear
entries.what: Develops AI compliance infrastructure for safety-critical industries. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: AirSafe.ai
entries.what: Detect-and-avoid technology for long-range drone flights. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: EvoWorkforce
entries.what: Develops physical-AI apps so advanced robots can do specialised industrial tasks. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Eryvo
entries.what: Intelligent interaction platform that turns websites into adaptive, conversational interfaces. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: BreastScreening-AI
entries.what: Uses AI to diagnose breast cancer. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: LusoScan AI
entries.what: AI middleware that pre-reads hospital imaging exams and flags urgent anomalies. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Medgical
entries.what: Health startup using AI to automate clinical records. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Neuroreviver
entries.what: Digital health startup using AI for neurological screening. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Abtrace
entries.what: Artificial intelligence against antimicrobial resistance. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Pahilabs
entries.what: Based in Coimbra by its own text, builds a passwordless authentication system that uses AI against phishing. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Labtech - IconsAI
entries.what: Building a new generation of AI and software development. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: Future Dynamics Systems
entries.what: Advanced technologies for defence systems, AI, drones and augmented reality. Listed on IPN's incubator companies page, which does not say which stage each is in.

entries.name: PACT incubation and cowork plans (inPACT physical, onPACT digital, cowork, premium)
entries.what: PACT lists four ways to join its ecosystem: physical incubation with a dedicated room, digital incubation with a company address, a cowork desk, or a premium plan with company headquarters and one cowork space. The page shows no prices. It says the park holds 55 companies.

entries.name: ÉvoraTech incubator (council-owned, run by ADRAL, inside PACT)
entries.what: A 705 square metre incubator for technology-based and innovative firms in their early stages, with shared services and a FabLab for prototyping. The page was updated on 8 May 2024.

entries.name: ADRAL: advice for entrepreneurs and the incubator network
entries.what: The regional development agency says it supports entrepreneurs from idea to market, helps find funding and prepare applications, and runs a network of incubators with desks in the municipalities.

entries.name: AlentEdge Office at PACT (intellectual property and business support)
entries.what: PACT's office helps with trademarks, patents and design registration through a partner, with a 15 percent discount for PACT ecosystem members on that partner's fees, and offers certified training courses.

entries.name: Universidade de Évora: start-ups and spin-offs
entries.what: The university's innovation division says it promotes the creation of university start-ups and supports spin-offs from its research with coaching and funding. The page was last published with 2020 data.

entries.name: Startup Portugal: national incubation network and founder guide
entries.what: The national start-up agency's site lists the national incubator network, a founder's guide and programmes for entrepreneurs. We did not find an Évora-specific page on it.

entries.name: Empresa na Hora (Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado, via ePortugal)
entries.what: A national service at counters called Empresa na Hora to set up private limited companies, single-member companies and public limited companies quickly. Updated 4 September 2026 on ePortugal. The page does not list the Évora counter.

entries.name: EIT Deep Tech Talent (European Union) into PACT's AIRA project
entries.what: The AIRA course and ideas contest on AI in robotics was funded by the European Union through EIT Deep Tech Talent. PACT's projects page also lists AI Robotics Academy among its active projects. The amount is not stated on the pages we read.

entries.name: NxN Data Centers into an Évora data centre
entries.what: Bought a 1 MW operating data centre in Évora and plans up to 100 million euros of investment in Portugal over three years.
entries.amount: up to 100 million euros across Portugal over three years

entries.name: Alentejo 2030, Horizon Europe, PRR and Interreg funds in PACT's projects
entries.what: PACT's projects page lists 15 active co-funded projects, such as ROBO-KNOT (Horizon Europe), Future Lab (Alentejo 2030) and CIRCULARTECH (PRR), and says the projects represent 16 million euros of investment. Only the AI in robotics project is clearly AI.
entries.amount: 16 million euros across all PACT projects, as PACT states

entries.name: Faro council: Desenvolvimento económico (Faro Invest)
entries.what: The council's economic development desk lists technological and business innovation as a priority and names spin-offs from the University of Algarve, strategic and individual investors and service entrepreneurs as its audiences. Meetings are by appointment.

entries.name: Faro council: business incubation (a business nest managed by ANJE)
entries.what: Spaces for microenterprises and emerging projects of young entrepreneurs. The page names no services, price, sector or application channel, and points to IEFP and CRIA at the University of Algarve.

entries.name: UALG TEC Campus
entries.what: Technology incubator and accelerator on UAlg's Penha campus in Faro, opened in 2022, mostly information technology.

entries.name: Ideias em Caixa (UAlg and CRIA)
entries.what: Business-idea competition: 40 ideas get maturation sessions and the top idea in each of eight categories wins 5,000 euros. Open to over 18s and firms under three years old (8th edition, 2024 to 2025).

entries.name: UAlg proof-of-concept programme (CRIA)
entries.what: Takes technology projects from maturity level 3 to 6 towards demonstration in a real setting. The June 2026 call closed on 10 July.

entries.name: Venture Lab by Algarve STP
entries.what: Free mentoring for 12 validated Algarve startups and SMEs, funded by Algarve 2030. The 2026 call closed on 24 June.

entries.name: Algarve Evolution
entries.what: Lists an incubator, the Founder2Founder growth programme and INOVA Algarve 3.0 for tourism firms adopting AI and robotics.

entries.name: International Sci-Tech Innovation Competition (information session at UALG TEC Campus, 21 July 2026)
entries.what: A China and Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries contest with prizes up to about 25 million euros across 100 projects, run by two chambers of commerce with Algarve Evolution. Winners can reach over 50 investment funds in the Greater Bay Area. No deadline stated.

entries.name: Horizon Europe, Teaming for Excellence (European Commission) into UAlgTec Heritage
entries.what: 15 million euros of the 31.5 million euro package for the University of Algarve's archaeology centre ICArEHB.

entries.name: Portugal Ventures into MTI (Managing The Intelligence)
entries.what: Invested more than half a million euros in MTI, a UAlg spin-off at UALG TEC Campus that automates hotel air conditioning. The source ties the original research to AI (genetic algorithms) but does not say how the product uses AI today.

entries.name: Algarve 2030 and Algarve Empreende 2026
entries.what: Regional programme money behind Venture Lab, UAlg's proof-of-concept programme, and the AI and robotics pilot for 15 tourism SMEs.

entries.name: PRR scholarships for the AuroraMed and UAlg AI course
entries.what: Recovery plan funding covered the full fee for selected participants of the April 2026 executive course on AI in health.

entries.name: expressTEC
entries.what: Faro biotech startup spun out of UAlg research, building an RNA-based test to guide cancer therapy, with machine-learning software that produces the clinical report.

entries.name: MTI (Managing The Intelligence)
entries.what: UAlg spin-off founded in October 2019 and based at UALG TEC Campus. Sensors and a web app switch off hotel room air conditioning when a window opens or a room is empty. Backed by Portugal Ventures.

entries.name: Incubadora Desnuclearizada do IPG (Guarda pole)
entries.what: The polytechnic's incubator network, with a pole on the Guarda campus and others in Mêda, Vouzela and São Pedro do Sul and São João da Pesqueira. Eight companies joined the Guarda pole in August 2025.

entries.name: Digital PME (IPG, ADSI, NERGA, Capital Douro)
entries.what: A two year project co-funded by COMPETE 2030 to help small firms and startups in the Centro region adopt advanced digital technologies, starting April 2026.

entries.name: Município da Guarda: Espaço Empresa / Apoio ao Investidor
entries.what: The council's business and investor desk, under its Investir section (Empresas, Apoio ao Investidor, Empreendedorismo). It lists support and incentives, company creation, training and information sessions and referral to support bodies, with no programme named. The Empreendedorismo page names no incubator.

entries.name: Policasulos (UPG nano-incubation space)
entries.what: Acceleration and incubation for business projects, in former classrooms where student or staff founding teams can set up.

entries.name: Poliempreende (UPG)
entries.what: Business-idea competition and support from creativity to company creation or patent filing, within the national polytechnic network. Open to students, graduates and teachers in teams with students or graduates. The 2025/2026 edition ran from May to June 2026 with a regional jury on 12 June. The page lists no prizes.

entries.name: UPG executive training in innovation and intellectual property (with Inventa)
entries.what: Hybrid evening programme launched in March 2026 on patents, trademarks, designs and technology transfer, aimed at researchers, entrepreneurs and municipal technicians. Startups in the UPG incubator asked for it.

entries.name: ARRISCA C, 15th national business-idea competition (announced by UPG)
entries.what: National competition for business ideas based on science and technology, open for applications until 18 December 2026 at 23:59, with cash prizes of up to 2,500 euros depending on category and service prizes such as incubation, mentoring, consulting, training and business plan support. Details and the form are on arriscac.pt, which we did not read.

entries.name: Portugal 2030, COMPETE 2030 into Digital PME
entries.what: 849,672 euros of the 999,614 euro project led by the polytechnic, with the partners adding the rest from their own funds.

entries.name: Empowered Startups (HQA Visa Program) into the Guarda incubator
entries.what: A programme partnership with the polytechnic brought foreign-backed startups into its incubator, among them A-G Transformer, a digital agriculture startup, reported on 2 April 2024. In May 2025 the incubator hosted three companies with North American capital, one with Indian capital and several with Portuguese investors. No amounts or investor names are given.

entries.name: Imo Harmonia (student project)
entries.what: AI platform for reading municipal master plans, made by polytechnic students, winner of the regional Poliempreende phase in 2025. We found no sign of a company behind it.

entries.name: Startup Leiria: incubation and acceleration
entries.what: Non-profit incubator and accelerator that says it supports entrepreneurs and companies from the idea stage. Its front page lists incubation and acceleration, hosting and business-address registration, and a coworking space in central Leiria. It also lists Link Her (a community for women entrepreneurs, news item of 23 October 2026), social-innovation projects and Academy for Impact. It publishes no formal application process or deadline.

entries.name: Startup Leiria: STRIDE 351 for international scale-ups
entries.what: Call run by Startup Leiria with C2 Capital Partners for technologically mature international scale-ups that want to set up in Portugal. Focus areas: defence and dual use, agrotech, industry and hardware, healthcare, high-growth services. Applications close on 18 November 2026. The article states no investment amount and does not use the name STRIDE 351 itself, so the link to the menu entry is our inference.

entries.name: Startup Leiria: Cowork and business-address hosting
entries.what: Office and coworking space in central Leiria, with support for registering a business address.

entries.name: Call Leiria Crescimento (Portugal Ventures, NERLEI, Banco Português de Fomento)
entries.what: PRR-funded call for Leiria-region companies, in its third edition in 2025 with investments of 250,000 to 1.5 million euros per company and applications from 8 April to 18 May 2025. Four Startup Leiria companies shared 5.5 million euros. We found no 2026 edition.

entries.name: Leiria council: Espaço Empresa and PRO Leiria
entries.what: The council's Economia section lists an Espaço Empresa desk, PRO Leiria economic development and the Monte Redondo business park. The pages we could read are menus without text, so we cannot say what each offers.

entries.name: Leiria Experience Lab (Startup Leiria with the council)
entries.what: Programme in which the council tests local startup products as first customer: it bought Leiria Concierge and Guide Sofia for 7,500 euros in total in 2026.

entries.name: Poliempreende (Politécnico de Leiria, becoming ULO)
entries.what: National higher-education entrepreneurship network programme to build entrepreneurial culture, develop business plans and reward the best projects. The page says over 813 participants and more than 58,000 euros in prizes across editions, and lists about 30 spin-off companies. It names no incubation or spin-off seal.

entries.name: NEXXT Leiria: Leiria Nexxt Ideas
entries.what: Ideas contest of the NEXXT Leiria event. The 2026 edition named ten winners from 42 applications, four of them AI projects.

entries.name: Portugal Ventures (Leiria Crescimento)
entries.what: Invested 5.5 million euros in four Startup Leiria companies in 2025: BHOUT, Glartek, Leadzai and Mantis AI. The article gives no per-company amounts.

entries.name: Portugal Ventures into Brainr
entries.what: Added 1.5 million euros to Brainr's seed round in July 2026.

entries.name: C2 Capital Partners into Brainr
entries.what: Led Brainr's record seed round of up to 11 million euros, announced in 2025.

entries.name: Call Leiria Crescimento (programme)
entries.what: PRR-funded programme run by Portugal Ventures with NERLEI and Banco Português de Fomento, with 250,000 to 1.5 million euros per company in its 2025 edition.

entries.name: Centro 2030 application for the Physical AI lab
entries.what: Startup Leiria's planned lab of nearly 2,000 square metres, about 1.7 million euros, depends on a Centro 2030 application still under review, aiming to open in 2027.

entries.name: Comcast NBCUniversal, Opus Investimentos and Portugal Ventures into Mantis-AI
entries.what: The investors named by the company's own profile article.

entries.name: Primal AI
entries.what: First AI spin-off of the Universidade de Leiria e Oeste, from the school of technology and management and CIIC. Builds AI into business and industrial software for SMEs.

entries.name: Brainr
entries.what: Leiria-based maker of AI-powered production software for food factories. Seed round of up to 11 million euros in 2025, extended by 1.5 million euros in July 2026.

entries.name: Mantis-AI
entries.what: Leiria start-up that analyses video with its own AI and machine learning models for broadcasters and producers. Investors named are Comcast NBCUniversal, Opus Investimentos and Portugal Ventures.

entries.name: Glartek
entries.what: Startup Leiria company that uses augmented reality, AI and IoT to optimise industrial tasks in real time. One of four firms that shared 5.5 million euros from Portugal Ventures in 2025.

entries.name: BHOUT
entries.what: Maker of a smart punching bag that analyses the user's movements, which the incubator's article says uses AI. Shared the 5.5 million euro Portugal Ventures round in 2025.

entries.name: Dimera
entries.what: Leiria company incubated at Startup Leiria that makes sustainable materials with AI and nanoengineering, and won an innovation category at the 7th Prémios Mares Circulares. The article does not say how the AI is applied.

entries.name: Leiria Concierge
entries.what: Winner of the 2026 Leiria Experience Lab. An AI assistant that builds personalised itineraries from natural-language requests, using the council's official tourism information, in Portuguese and English.

entries.name: Guide Sofia
entries.what: Second place in the 2026 Leiria Experience Lab. An AI platform that turns a phone into a guide, with a first audio tour of Leiria Castle due as a prototype by end of August 2026.

entries.name: Opsivision Leiria, Sndora, e-Security and Bora, Leiria? (Leiria Nexxt Ideas 2026 winners)
entries.what: Four awarded projects where AI is central: video-surveillance analysis, a sales and payments platform with AI tools, authenticity checks with biometrics and AI, and personalised city itineraries. The article does not say whether each is already a company.

entries.name: Portugal Ventures (Leiria Crescimento call)
entries.what: Invested 5.5 million euros in four Startup Leiria companies in 2025 through a PRR-funded call run with NERLEI and Banco Português de Fomento, and 1.5 million euros more in Brainr in 2026.

entries.name: C2 Capital Partners
entries.what: Venture fund that led Brainr's seed round of up to 11 million euros in 2025. Startup Leiria's STRIDE 351 call for international scale-ups is also described as run with it.

entries.name: Unicorn Factory Lisboa: Incubation Program
entries.what: Founder-driven programme from pre-seed to seed, with no equity taken, fully online and no registered company needed. It cites over 1,000 startups supported since 2012 and over 200 mentors. The next batch closes in early December 2026 (its pages say 1 and 3 December).

entries.name: Unicorn Factory Lisboa: Active Programs and thematic hubs
entries.what: Open calls for mobility and cleantech, a global scaling cohort and agritech and foodtech acceleration, plus membership programmes with partners for AI (Google, Microsoft and the Center for Responsible AI), cleantech, healthtech and industrials.

entries.name: AIhub membership and coworking
entries.what: AI community with tiers from free (Discovery) to paid (Immersion and Catalyst), coworking from a 15 euro day pass and private offices. Prices as published, plus VAT.

entries.name: Unicorn Factory Lisboa: Soft Landing Program
entries.what: Listed on the hub's menu as support for founders setting up in Lisbon. On 17 November the menu entry links to an application form on a Microsoft forms address, not to a page of terms, and the guessed address /soft-landing/ returns 404, so we still cannot state its terms.

entries.name: Startup Portugal One Stop Shop (Lisbon office at Cais Português, Pavilhão de Portugal)
entries.what: Centralised information and personalised support, online and in person, for those who want to found, operate and scale a business from Portugal, with offices in Lisboa and Porto.

entries.name: Startup Portugal: programmes and incubator network (RNi)
entries.what: National agency for the startup ecosystem. Runs the monthly Above & Beyond Hangouts, the Tech Foundry Portugal deep tech programme and Road 2 Web Summit, and keeps the national incubator network RNi.

entries.name: Empresa na Hora (Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado, via gov.pt)
entries.what: Counter service to create quota companies, single-member quota companies and public limited companies quickly. The gov.pt page was updated on 4 September 2026 and names the registry institute as responsible.

entries.name: Índico Capital Partners and Lince Capital into Beyond Vision
entries.what: Co-led the funding round of a Lisbon drone maker that plans to speed up AI and swarm technology.

entries.name: Armilar Venture Partners into DOJO AI
entries.what: Led the April 2026 seed round of an agent-based marketing company with a Lisbon base and a place in Unicorn Factory's AIhub.

entries.name: Horizon Europe Teaming for Excellence and national funds into INESC-ID's AI centre
entries.what: 13 million euros from Horizon Europe plus 14.2 million of national money for the sustainable and trustworthy AI centre.

entries.name: University of Lisbon's own investment in two AI data centres
entries.what: Over 20 million euros for computing for AI and research data in Lisbon and Oeiras, open to companies and startups, due by 2028.

entries.name: Banco Português de Fomento: IFIC call for AI adoption (national)
entries.what: The state development bank received over 3,700 applications to the AI call of its innovation and competitiveness instrument, with proposed investment of 801 million euros, and sent its first decisions on 5 February 2026. The call is national, the page does not place the winners in Lisboa.

entries.name: Unicorn Factory Lisboa investor network
entries.what: The Incubation Program page cites over 150 investors and over 200 mentors in its network, and the site shows a partners section for corporates and investors. It names no individual fund.

entries.name: Augusta Labs
entries.what: Lisbon applied AI lab for enterprises, private equity and government, valued at 50 million euros after its first round.

entries.name: DOJO AI
entries.what: Agent-based marketing platform with headquarters in London and Lisbon, which raised a 6 million dollar seed round.

entries.name: Armilar Venture Partners
entries.what: Venture fund that led DOJO AI's April 2026 seed round. The page we opened does not state its base city.

entries.name: AgentifAI
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. Conversational AI for customer care with a voice-first assistant. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: Coalex.ai
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI automation with human oversight, aimed at compliance risk. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: Granter
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI platform that matches companies with grants and drafts applications. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: jsonify
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. An AI tool that autonomously finds, extracts and syncs online data. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: Keymate360
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI-powered key account management. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: Mantis AI
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. Turns raw video into organised content. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: NeuralShift
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. Early-stage startup that integrates AI into lawyers' daily work. Also named in the Center for Responsible AI consortium. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: noan
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI system that gives a team one source of truth. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: Noxus
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. Platform to deploy AI company-wide without building from scratch. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: pleez
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. Uses delivery data and AI to manage restaurants and sales. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: rosent
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI recruiting platform for sourcing candidates. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: SentiVue
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI platform for customer touchpoints and loyalty. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: SparkNow
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI platform that summarises expert insights. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: talka
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. Extracts insights from video and voice conversations. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: Visor.ai
entries.what: Listed as a member of Unicorn Factory Lisboa's AIhub community. AI platform that automates customer service interactions. The page does not give each firm's headquarters.

entries.name: NERA, the regional business association (Loulé)
entries.what: Business support, legal advice, professional training, economic information, a business centre and space rental, and coworking.

entries.name: Ninho de Empresas de Loulé (IEFP)
entries.what: A public business and technology incubator, as BeAlgarve's directory classes it.

entries.name: Loulé Design Lab (Loulé Criativo)
entries.what: The municipal creative and technology incubator and coworking space.

entries.name: CASULO, social innovation incubator
entries.what: Listed for Loulé by BeAlgarve as an incubator of social innovation.

entries.name: Algarve AI Agents
entries.what: An AI community covering Faro and Loulé, as BeAlgarve lists it. No page of its own found yet.

entries.name: Loulé and Faro multi-technology centre, Estádio Algarve (planned)
entries.what: A tendered centre of about 2,235 square metres for companies and startups. Proposals were due on 2 November 2026 and the work has 12 months to run.

entries.name: Algarve 2030 regional programme
entries.what: Co-finances half of the more than 3.5 million euro Estádio Algarve technology centre and the Inova Algarve 3.0 AI and robotics pilot for tourism firms.
entries.amount: more than 3.5 million euros total, 50% Algarve 2030

entries.name: European funds behind SPIC's AI.EVENT
entries.what: RTP says SPIC's AI platform for reading audience reactions has had European funding. It names no programme or amount.

entries.name: Re-Source 3.0 (Sociedade Ponto Verde) behind ALGAR's AI tool
entries.what: The programme under which ALGAR and NILG.AI built the AI recycling-point tool. One report puts the investment at 50 thousand euros.

entries.name: NILG.AI (partner of ALGAR)
entries.what: Start-up incubated at UPTEC, the University of Porto's science park, that co-built ALGAR's AI recycling-point tool. Not a Loulé firm: it is listed as ALGAR's partner.

entries.name: Gabinete de Empreendedorismo (council business desk)
entries.what: Created January 2022. Prepares funding applications for businesses and public bodies, tracks funding lines, prepares feasibility studies and supports investors.

entries.name: Incubadora de Empresas de Monchique (IEM)
entries.what: Individual, accompanied support for local entrepreneurs, online follow-up sessions and signposting to open funding calls. Pre-registration at the Espaço Jovem next to the Monchique parish council. No AI programme is named.

entries.name: Invisible CFO
entries.what: Portuguese fintech founded in 2024 and based in Monchique, a digital finance provider for small businesses and freelancers. By its own account it combines AI, automation and a human team, and says 300,000 euros of EU funding helped develop its AI and automation applications. Named an Impact Startup 2025.

entries.name: NERPOR business incubation
entries.what: The business association launched a project in January 2026 to incubate 12 companies in its own premises, with a contract per firm, workspace, and a support desk that helps with EU funding applications and networking. It may grow by 20 rooms in three years. No sector is named and the source does not say how it is financed.

entries.name: BioBIP, the polytechnic's business incubator
entries.what: Takes applications through an online form and answers in about 30 days, with a preference for technology-based projects. It has a FabLab with milling and digital fabrication equipment, and counts 78 supported companies on its homepage.

entries.name: C.BIP, the polytechnic's cultural and creative incubator
entries.what: Opened in 2023 in a rehabilitated building in the historic centre, with 830,000 euros from the council, coworking, meeting rooms and applications on a rolling basis. It targets non-technology firms in arts, culture and heritage, so it is not a route for an AI startup. The same polytechnic's incubators C.BIP and BioBIP were both admitted to the national RNi network in the Tech category, per BioBIP.

entries.name: Espaço Empresa and the Parque Industrial (Câmara Municipal de Portalegre)
entries.what: The Espaço Empresa is a one-stop desk for firms run with national agencies (AMA, IAPMEI, AICEP), open on working days from 08:30 to 16:00, with a link to the T-Invest form for Portalegre. The council's industrial park offers lots of 1,000 to 10,000 square metres, with a Ninho de Empresas startup centre among its infrastructure. The page was last updated in January 2023.

entries.name: Industrial Portugal Gateway (Luso Defense Group with NERPOR)
entries.what: A single coordination point for firms investing in Portalegre in defence, security and dual-use technology, covering licensing, financing, recruitment and finding suppliers. It targets SMEs, startups and component suppliers, and its public launch was set for 25 September 2026.

entries.name: Empresa na Hora (Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado)
entries.what: National service at a registry counter to create a limited company, sole-shareholder company or public limited company quickly. gov.pt shows the page as updated on 4 September 2026 and does not list counters by town.

entries.name: FEDER under ALT2030 into AI4PRIME
entries.what: Funds the university's AI for farming and livestock project, 197,754.85 euros eligible cost, 168,091.62 euros for the Portalegre side.

entries.name: FEDER under ALT2030 into EmoCare
entries.what: Funds the university's generative-AI student mental health platform, 106,936.75 euros eligible cost, 90,896.23 euros for the Portalegre side.

entries.name: Alentejo 2030 regional programme into CIMAA public-sector training
entries.what: About 381,000 euros, co-financed by the EU, for training 1,195 public workers with AI among nine themes.

entries.name: EU funds into CIC Alentejo (Campo Maior)
entries.what: About one million euros in cost, with the Campo Maior council covering the 15 percent national counterpart. The exact fund is not named in the article we read.

entries.name: RNi Portugal Incubators (managed by Startup Portugal)
entries.what: National incubator network that admitted BioBIP and C.BIP in the Tech category. The page names no funding amount.

entries.name: StartUP Portimão, business incubator
entries.what: The council's incubator, part of the Centro de Negócios de Portimão at the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, for projects with growth potential in smart cities (energy, mobility, tourism, governance, quality of life). It has an apply section on its site and a services page.

entries.name: StartUP Portimão acceleration programme
entries.what: The 7th edition of the incubator's accelerator for entrepreneurs and business projects in the Algarve: skills, stronger business models and new market opportunities. Applications closed on 28 October 2026, with a first online bootcamp on 2 and 3 November and a second in person in Portimão on 24 and 25 November 2026. No AI theme is stated.

entries.name: Portimão Cowork (council shared workspace)
entries.what: A council shared workspace open to people and organisations with an idea, project or business that adds value to the local economy, with a continued regime and a daily regime, each with its own form and operating rules.

entries.name: Pitch & Match
entries.what: A session at StartUP Portimão's ninth anniversary on 10 August 2026 meant to connect entrepreneurs, business people, mentors and potential investors. No investor organisation is named in the report.

entries.name: Mentors and partner network of StartUP Portimão
entries.what: In 2022 the incubator reported more than 40 mentors, more than 45 partner entities and 25 startups hosted. Its site has sections for national and local partners, an advisory board and mentors.

entries.name: Digital-transformation grant, call ALGARVE-2025-13
entries.what: Approved investment for the council's digital services, covering infrastructure, security, Wi-Fi and automation, with AI listed among the project areas.

entries.name: Regional funding call for the UAlg technology campus
entries.what: A call of 10 million euros at 60% funding, with the application to ALGARVE 2030 expected around February 2025, for a campus whose focus areas are digital, data and AI. Funding was not fully secured at the time of the report.
entries.amount: 10 million euros available in the call

entries.name: Fundo Ambiental, EMARP leak-control projects
entries.what: Funds two leak-detection projects of the municipal water company, including the AI acoustic loggers.

entries.name: CRESC Algarve 2020 (FEDER) funding for the Celerator technology hub
entries.what: 4 million euros of European funds in a 7.2 million euro mobility and energy technology hub beside the Autódromo, run by Parkalgar and UAlg. No AI work is stated.

entries.name: Guepardo
entries.what: Listed by the StartUP Portimão incubator as developing V2X (vehicle-to-everything) and AI products to improve road mobility and traffic coordination. The incubator's list is undated (its footer says 2023) and does not separate current residents from alumni. We found no independent reporting on its products, funding or deployments.

entries.name: UPTEC (Science and Technology Park of the University of Porto)
entries.what: Incubates startups including Granter and the AI startups in the map, and hosts the BSC AI Factory round at Asprela II.

entries.name: BSC AI Factory incubation programme (FCT and CNCA)
entries.what: Free supercomputing access, mentoring and training for EU AI startups and SMEs with a Portuguese tax number, up to 10 years old and under 20 staff. The 2026 round (5 October to 30 March 2027) is closed, and selected firms use the coworking space three times a week.

entries.name: START Rise AI Challenge (Start Campus with Porto Business School)
entries.what: A contest that visited Porto, Faro and Lisbon. The 2026 final was on 29 May, and the top prize was space at the Start Campus data centre in Sines plus cloud credits.

entries.name: Câmara Municipal do Porto: Divisão Municipal de Empreendedorismo
entries.what: The council's entrepreneurship division says it runs action plans, conferences and forums to encourage new companies and attract startups, and links the city's ecosystem players. The page lists a contact block that did not show in the text we read.

entries.name: Porto Innovation Hub (council platform)
entries.what: Platform launched by the council in 2016 to strengthen the city's innovation ecosystem, with open events such as City Café and visits.

entries.name: Startup Portugal, Porto office
entries.what: National non-profit that opened a Porto office in July 2024. Its agreement with the council allows a municipal derrama tax exemption for companies it recognises as startups or scaleups based in Porto, as reported then.

entries.name: UPTEC incubation (University of Porto)
entries.what: Takes business ideas, young startups and corporate innovation teams, with offices, laboratories, coworking or virtual membership, mentoring, events and perks. Open to people outside the university too, per its application page.

entries.name: ScaleUp Porto (council programme, with Porto Digital)
entries.what: A coordinated programme inside the city's innovation and competitiveness strategy, with a startup investment toolkit made with Porto Business School. Its own news page we read stops in August 2024.

entries.name: Balcão Empresa na Hora (national, any counter)
entries.what: Registry service that sets up a limited company at one counter in one visit, with all partners present. A normal request costs 360 euros, and it works at any counter whatever the future seat.

entries.name: ScaleUp Porto programmes (council)
entries.what: Council programme lists Doing Business, Masterclasses, Start & Scale Week, SCALE.CITIES, Scaleup for Europe and Open Calls (August 2026). Its news page shows items to 16 November 2026, so it is current, unlike what an earlier page read suggested.

entries.name: 33N Ventures
entries.what: Porto-based venture fund that took part in the 270 million euro Exein round in September 2026.

entries.name: 3XP Global (Impact Innovation Fund) into Granter
entries.what: Led Granter's 1.6 million euro round under the FdCR venture programme managed by Banco Português de Fomento, with Celtis Venture Partners, Gateway Ventures and Deel. The investors' own base cities are not stated on the page.

entries.name: SMARTEX.AI funding (Startup Genome listing)
entries.what: Startup Genome's Porto page lists a 40 million dollar raise by this industrial AI startup in May 2025. We did not open the funding announcement.

entries.name: BSC AI Factory in Portugal (FCT and CNCA)
entries.what: Public programme giving AI startups free supercomputing time, based at UPTEC for the 2026 to 2027 round.

entries.name: Ten investors into Savearth
entries.what: UPTEC startup Savearth raised the sum from ten investors, who are not named on the page.

entries.name: FCT through the recovery plan (PRR) into CitiLink
entries.what: Funded the CitiLink project of INESC TEC, the University of Porto and UBI from 2024 to early 2026. The amount is not stated.

entries.name: Recovery plan (PRR) into the AMALIA language model
entries.what: Paid for the state-backed national model, which Porto teams helped build. The sum is for the whole national project, not for Porto.

entries.name: CMU Portugal programme into i3S NeuroSAFE
entries.what: Exploratory project grant of about 100,000 euros for AI methods to control neurons safely, led from the i3S institute in Porto.

entries.name: Granter
entries.what: UPTEC startup founded in 2023. AI platform that finds public funding for SMEs, prepares applications and manages funded projects. Raised 1.6 million euros in November 2026.

entries.name: DigestAID
entries.what: University of Porto spin-off at UPTEC, founded in 2021, building AI tools for digestive health, including video analysis of capsule endoscopy (as reported in October 2025).

entries.name: GynoAID
entries.what: UPTEC startup founded in 2023 with an AI platform to detect and tell apart lesions in the female genital tract, with accuracy the article puts above 95 percent (the company's own claim).

entries.name: Scemai
entries.what: UPTEC startup founded in 2021 selling AI for industry. Its assistant plans factory-floor work and shows machine status, capacity, energy and staffing.

entries.name: Adeci
entries.what: UPTEC startup founded in 2023 that uses AI to forecast restaurant sales and orders up to 31 days ahead, reporting about 92 percent accuracy.
